paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on how to enrich students’ knowledge of traditional Chinese culture. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设大学报纸正在邀请学生为下一期的报纸投稿，讨论如何丰富学生对中国传统文化的了解。您现在需要写一篇论文以供提交。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: When Toni Morrison died in 2019, the world lost one of its most influential authors. But Morrison was not an early success. Her first novel was not published until she was 39, and her last appeared when she was
84. And Morrison was not 26 in this regard. Numerous writers produce masterpieces well into their 70s

and beyond. Such 27 accomplishments highlight an important point. Our capacity to speak, write and learn new vocabulary does not seem to 28 with age. Our eyesight may dim and our recall may weaken, but, by comparison, our ability to produce and to 29 language is well preserved into older adulthood.

Indeed, the latest research that has emerged on language and aging shows that language mastery is a 30 that we begin as infants and continue on for the rest of our lives. Some aspects of our language abilities, such as our knowledge of word meanings, 31 improve during middle and late adulthood. One study, for example, found that adults over sixty had an average vocabulary size of over 21,000 words. The researchers also studied a 32 of college students and found that their average vocabulary contained 33 16,000 words. In another study, older adults, with an average age of 75, 34 better than participants in their youth or middle years on tasks that required them to determine the meaning of words. Thus, language seems to be a skill that, contrary to what many might 35 , does not weaken with age.

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: If we care about plastic waste, why won’t we stop drinking bottled water?
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果我们关心塑料垃圾，为什么我们不停止饮用瓶装水呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: We have all seen the damage plastic waste is doing around the world, but sales of bottled water have continued to grow.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们都看到塑料垃圾在世界各地造成的破坏，但瓶装水的销量仍在持续增长。

paragraphs.sourceText: A) For all the innovation and choice that define the food and drink industries, if you want to make money, you could do a lot worse than fill a bottle with water and sell it. A litre of tap water, the stuff we have cleverly piped into our homes, costs less than half a penny. A litre of bottled water can cost well over a pound, especially for something fancy that has been sucked through a mountain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答）对于定义食品和饮料行业的所有创新和选择，如果你想赚钱，你可以做比装满一瓶水然后出售更糟糕的事情。一升自来水，我们巧妙地通过管道输送到家里的水，成本不到半便士。一升瓶装水的价格远远超过一磅，特别是对于从山上吸来的奇特水来说。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Yet the bottled water market is livelier than ever. It defies our increasing awareness of the harm plastics do to the environment and a broader, growing sense that something has to change. Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year, an increase of 7%, according to the latest figures from the market analyst Kantar. Separate data from other analysts show that last year the British consumed more than 2.2 billion litres of bottled water, including “take-home” and “on-the-go” products. That’s an annual rise in volume of 8.5%.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 然而，瓶装水市场比以往任何时候都更加活跃。它违背了我们对塑料对环境危害的日益认识，以及对某些事情必须改变的更广泛、日益增长的认识。根据市场分析公司 Kantar 的最新数据，去年英国的销售额达到创纪录的 5.584 亿英镑，增长 7%。其他分析师的单独数据显示，去年英国人消耗了超过 22 亿升瓶装水，其中包括“带回家”和“随身携带”的产品。销量每年增长 8.5%。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Environmental campaigners are struggling to understand why nations blessed with clean tap water grow only fonder of the bottle. “It’s very surprising to me,” says Sam Chetan-Walsh, a political adviser at Greenpeace and campaigner against ocean plastic. “Public awareness has never been higher, but the message is not quite reaching all the people it needs to.” Where it is heard, the message is causing concern. Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuels to make and ship. Additionally, single-use plastics of all types are polluting our cities and seas. Numerous documentaries have shown how plastic is ultimately killing wildlife.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 环保人士正在努力理解为什么拥有清洁自来水的国家却更喜欢瓶子。 “这让我感到非常惊讶，”绿色和平组织政治顾问兼反对海洋塑料活动人士萨姆·切坦-沃尔什 (Sam Chetan-Walsh) 说。 “公众意识从未如此之高，但信息并没有完全传达给所有需要的人。”在听到这一消息的地方，该消息引起了人们的关注。塑料水瓶的制造和运输需要大量的化石燃料。此外，各种类型的一次性塑料正在污染我们的城市和海洋。许多纪录片都展示了塑料如何最终杀死野生动物。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Moves against various plastics have gathered pace, from shopping bags to straws and plastic-lined coffee cups. Chetan-Walsh argues that bottled water is different because the alternatives are so obvious. “If a product that is so nakedly unnecessary can exist, then the whole system is failing,” he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）反对各种塑料的行动已经加快，从购物袋到吸管和塑料衬里的咖啡杯。切坦-沃尔什认为，瓶装水与众不同，因为替代品非常明显。 “如果存在一种完全没有必要的产品，那么整个系统就会失败，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Hope is not entirely out of reach. The rate of growth has begun to ease (sales were up 7% in the year, compared with 8% the previous year).
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 希望并非完全遥不可及。增长率开始放缓（当年销售额增长了 7%，而上年为 8%）。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) But even if large numbers of people are quitting bottled water because of care for the environment, others are taking it up. The introduction of the “sugar tax” on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water, while health awareness has boosted its desirability. Tap water consumption is growing at roughly the same pace (UK consumers still drink almost three times as much tap water as bottled water).
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 但即使很多人因为保护环境而放弃瓶装水，其他人也在开始使用。对果汁和苏打饮料征收“糖税”促使更多人购买瓶装水，而健康意识也提高了人们对瓶装水的需求。自来水消耗量以大致相同的速度增长（英国消费者饮用的自来水几乎是瓶装水的三倍）。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) So the plastic tide only creeps higher. The industry is quick to point out that all its bottles are recyclable. “But collection rates are, at the most generous estimates, 56%, so the actual recycling rate will be lower than that,” Chetan-Walsh says. And while bottles may be recyclable, very few are made of recycled plastic. One water bottle company launched recycled half-litre “eco” bottles alongside its standard bottles. Another has pledged to use only recycled plastic across its range by 2025. Chetan-Walsh believes in a ban on single-use bottles. Bans do exist in some places. Organisers of a famous music festival announced that water bottles will not be sold this summer. San Francisco has banned them from city property and events. Last year, the UK government set out plans to ban single-use plastic from its estate.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 因此，塑料浪潮只会愈演愈烈。该行业很快指出，其所有瓶子都是可回收的。 “但根据最慷慨的估计，收集率为 56%，因此实际回收率将低于这个数字，”Chetan-Walsh 说。虽然瓶子可能是可回收的，但很少有瓶子是由回收塑料制成的。一家水瓶公司在其标准瓶的同时推出了回收的半升“生态”瓶。另一个公司承诺到 2025 年，其产品系列中将仅使用再生塑料。Chetan-Walsh 主张禁止使用一次性瓶子。有些地方确实存在禁令。一个著名音乐节的组织者宣布今年夏天将不再出售水瓶。旧金山已禁止他们进入城市财产和活动。去年，英国政府制定了禁止在其庄园内使用一次性塑料的计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Water bottlers, unsurprisingly, don’t support bans. But they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins. Last month one chief executive of a water bottling company said that bans would “result in greater consumption of sugary drinks, adding to all the health dangers of obesity, diabetes and tooth decay”. Kinvara Carey, general manager of an association of the biggest bottled water manufacturers, cites a survey in which people were asked what they would do if bottled water were not available. “Forty-four per cent would buy another drink, which is not great, 14% would go without and 4.5% said they would find a fountain,” she says. “The choice is important.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 毫不奇怪，水装瓶商不支持禁令。但他们引发的是对健康而非利润率的担忧。上个月，一家水瓶装公司的一位首席执行官表示，禁令将“导致含糖饮料的消费量增加，从而增加肥胖、糖尿病和蛀牙等健康危险”。最大瓶装水制造商协会的总经理金瓦拉·凯里（Kinvara Carey）引用了一项调查，其中人们被问及如果没有瓶装水他们会做什么。 “44% 的人会购买另一种饮料，这不太好，14% 的人会不喝，4.5% 的人表示他们会找到一个喷泉，”她说。 “选择很重要。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) What if fountains were more numerous, and tap water more clearly available in cafes, restaurants and elsewhere? Dozens of fountains are being installed in London. There are similar initiatives elsewhere. Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water in the first place, fountains were an urban fixture. Greenpeace, among others, is also pushing for a “deposit return” scheme. This would mean tax on bottled water would be refunded to customers who returned the plastic for recycling.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 如果喷泉数量更多，并且咖啡馆、餐馆和其他地方更容易获得自来水会怎么样？伦敦正在安装数十个喷泉。其他地方也有类似的举措。在塑料和营销让人们认为他们首先需要瓶装水之前，喷泉是城市的固定设施。绿色和平组织等也在推动“存款返还”计划。这意味着瓶装水税将退还给退回塑料进行回收的顾客。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Even if bottled water sales are growing slightly more slowly, the industry is racing to adapt to changing concerns and tastes. Flavoured water is booming: sales of the sparkling variety shot up by 20%, according to the latest analyst data. Meanwhile, international water brands, as well as a range of new companies, are selling high-end reusable bottles. And if you must fill them with tap water, why not add flavouring?
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 即使瓶装水销量增长稍慢，该行业仍在竞相适应不断变化的关注点和口味。调味水正在蓬勃发展：根据最新的分析师数据，该类型气泡水的销量猛增了 20%。与此同时，国际水品牌以及一系列新公司正在销售高端可重复使用的瓶子。如果必须用自来水填充，为什么不添加调味剂呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: K) As the owner of multiple sugary drink brands and bottled water, PepsiCo is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts. Last year, the company bought SodaStream (a drinks company that sells machines for making tap water bubbly and then consumers add flavours) for $3.2 billion. It also launched a range of fancy bottles that work with tap water and flavour packets. The bottle is reusable. The packets? Not so much, and, yes, they are made of plastic, although the company invites users to post them back for recycling.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 作为多个含糖饮料品牌和瓶装水的所有者，百事公司面临着健康和环境方面的挑战。去年，该公司以 32 亿美元收购了 SodaStream（一家饮料公司，销售使自来水起泡的机器，然后消费者添加口味）。它还推出了一系列适用于自来水和调味包的精美瓶子。该瓶子可重复使用。数据包？没那么多，而且，是的，它们是由塑料制成的，尽管该公司邀请用户将它们寄回以供回收。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) As is so often the case, clever marketing can beat reason; awareness is rarely enough. “There is always this kind of slip between concern, intent and changed behaviour,” says Giles Quick, an analyst of bottled water. “The best example is five a day, the recommendation to have at least five portions of fruit and vegetables every day. Almost everyone is aware of this, but something like 15% of us achieve it.” Unless a far-reaching bottle ban does come into force, it will be up to consumers to not only demand change — but to act themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 正如经常出现的情况一样，聪明的营销可以打败理性；意识还不够。 “关注、意图和行为改变之间总是存在这种偏差，”瓶装水分析师贾尔斯·奎克说。 “最好的例子是每天五份，建议每天至少吃五份水果和蔬菜。几乎每个人都意识到这一点，但大约 15% 的人做到了。”除非影响深远的瓶装禁令真正生效，否则消费者不仅要要求改变，还要采取行动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Judging from the slowing rate of sales growth, there is still hope to combat bottled water.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 从销售增速放缓来看，打击瓶装水仍有希望。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Bottled water manufacturers base their arguments against bans of plastic bottles on health concerns rather than on profits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 瓶装水制造商反对塑料瓶禁令的理由是基于健康问题而不是利润。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Sales of bottled water in Britain hit a record high last year even though people are increasingly aware that plastics are environmentally unfriendly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 尽管人们越来越意识到塑料对环境不友好，但去年英国瓶装水的销量创下了历史新高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. It often happens that people can lack reason when faced with skillful marketing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 当人们面对巧妙的营销时，常常会缺乏理性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. One city on the west coast of America has banned single-use bottles from its property and events.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 美国西海岸的一座城市禁止在其财产和活动中使用一次性瓶子。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Manufacturing and shipping of plastic water bottles consume a tremendous amount of fossil fuels.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 塑料水瓶的制造和运输消耗大量化石燃料。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. One large beverage company has adapted its operations when confronted with challenges from health and environmental advocates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 一家大型饮料公司在面临健康和环境倡导者的挑战时调整了其运营方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Bottled water is considerably more expensive than tap water.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 瓶装水比自来水贵得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Fountains could be seen in cities before bottled water became popular.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 在瓶装水流行之前，城市里就可以看到喷泉。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. More people have taken to bottled water because of their health awareness.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 出于健康意识，越来越多的人开始使用瓶装水。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people. A tipping point was reached in 2020 when human-made materials — such as steel, concrete and plastic — were found to weigh more than all life on Earth. Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits that the Woodland Trust successfully lobbied for it to be prescribed by doctors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人类与自然联系的减弱可能有利于经济增长，但对人类不利。 2020 年达到了一个转折点，当时人类制造的材料（例如钢铁、混凝土和塑料）被发现比地球上所有生命的重量还要重。继续种植混凝土森林而不是真正的森林是短视的。仅仅呆在最近的树林里就对健康大有裨益，以至于林地信托基金成功游说医生开这种药。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. It is not a moment too soon that teenagers will be able to take a natural history test, given that for decades children have been able to name more video game characters than wildlife species.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，自然世界的奇迹和美丽却从流行文化中消失了。研究人员发现，20 世纪 50 年代热门歌曲中每三个与自然相关的单词，50 年后只有略多于一个。鉴于几十年来，孩子们能够说出的电子游戏角色比野生动物物种还要多，所以现在青少年能够参加自然历史测试还为时过早。

paragraphs.sourceText: Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a “right to grow” law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil — while producing food sustainably.
paragraphs.translationZh: 补救这种社会疾病的一部分是议会通过一项“种植权”法律，允许任何人将未充分利用的公共空间变成蔬菜和水果园。这个想法是让人们重新接触土壤——同时可持续地生产食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived (使复活) by green-thumbed (有园艺才能的) social media influencers who defy local U.S. regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 蔬菜种植有着令人尊敬的传统。 1649 年 4 月，当地人通过在英格兰南部的公共土地上种植蔬菜来应对高价格和粮食短缺。投掷种子炸弹将空地变成绿色的做法在 20 世纪 70 年代的纽约兴起，并被那些擅长园艺的（有园艺天赋的）社交媒体影响者重新复活，他们在一场针对城市丑陋地点的战争中无视美国当地法规。

paragraphs.sourceText: Apart from the urgent task of providing more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can’t afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens connect what we eat to where it comes from — the means of production, if you will. They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community. Plants are also, of course, our first defence against species loss and climate change. Such planting is a small step for humanity — in the right direction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除了为那些越来越买不起的人提供更健康的营养物质这一紧迫任务之外，公共水果和蔬菜园还将我们所吃的东西与其来源联系起来——如果你愿意的话，也可以说是生产资料。它们可以让不可爱的空间变得可爱，将实用性和美观结合起来，并有助于促进社区意识。当然，植物也是我们抵御物种丧失和气候变化的第一道屏障。这种种植是人类朝着正确方向迈出的一小步。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Engineering in the U.S. has long been a male-dominated profession. Fifty years ago, it looked like that might change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在美国，工程学长期以来一直是男性主导的职业。五十年前，情况似乎可能会改变。

paragraphs.sourceText: In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%. Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. But that’s not what happened. Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000.
paragraphs.translationZh: 1970年，工程学专业的女性比例还不到1%。 1979 年，这个数字是 9%。许多人希望女性能够继续以同样的速度进入该领域。但事实并非如此。如今，只有 21% 的工程专业学生是女性，这一数字自 2000 年以来基本没有变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: I am a historian who, along with my colleagues, surveyed 251 women engineers who graduated from college in the 1970s. These pioneers reflected on the challenges they faced — and had advice for women entering the field today.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我是一名历史学家，与我的同事一起调查了 251 名 251 名 20 世纪 70 年代大学毕业的女工程师。这些先驱者反思了他们所面临的挑战，并为当今进入该领域的女性提出了建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: One survey taker explained, “The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 一位受访者解释说：“对我来说，最大的挑战是继续相信自己，因为我得到的所有信息都是，我永远不会像男性那样受到认真对待、晋升或加薪，因为他们的资格显然不如我，也不像我那么聪明。”

paragraphs.sourceText: A chemical engineer who worked in manufacturing agreed, “You have to prove yourself just because you are female. And you have to work twice as hard!”
paragraphs.translationZh: 一位从事制造业的化学工程师也表示同意：“因为你是女性，你就必须证明自己。而且你必须加倍努力！”

paragraphs.sourceText: A civil engineer said, “We are ‘women engineers.’ People don’t refer to a man as a ‘man engineer’ — he’s an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don’t truly belong.” Another civil engineer stated, “On many levels, you’re never quite one of the group.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 一位土木工程师说：“我们是‘女工程师’。人们不会称男人为‘男工程师’——他只是一名工程师。我们不断被提醒，我们并不真正属于这里。”另一位土木工程师表示：“在很多层面上，你永远都不是团队中的一员。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Women also talked about family caregiving responsibilities. A retired vice president from a major chemical company stated, “Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children, then they struggle to balance work and family — and compete with men who don’t have the same household responsibilities.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 女性还谈到了照顾家庭的责任。一家大型化工公司的退休副总裁表示：“年轻的女工程师在有了孩子之前一直处于平等的地位，然后她们就很难平衡工作和家庭，并与没有同样家庭责任的男性竞争。”

paragraphs.sourceText: But over the years things have changed a lot. Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但这些年来，情况发生了很大变化。年轻女性工程师更容易被接受，主要是因为她们的数量更多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. A mechanical engineer said, “It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多女工程师称赞她们所选择的职业所带来的好处。一位制造业项目经理表示，工程学是最好的学位。一位机械工程师说：“它会让你灵活地做几乎任何事情。看到你所做的事情的效果也很令人满意。”
